paper_title: On Equivalent Characterizations of the Polynomial Hierarchy in Abstract Models of Computation
statement: We conjecture that the assumption that R is of finite type is not strictly necessary because there are structures R of infinite type for which SAT(R) is NP(R) complete, as shown in [34, 24]. However, we have a strong intuition that the existence of an effective encoding for R is a necessary condition for SAT(R) to be in NP(R) because if there is an operation of R that R-machines cannot decode, then R-machines should not be able to test the truth of formulas with this operation. Indeed, the known infinite-type structures for which SAT(R) is NP(R)-complete are Megiddo extensions of finite-type structures, and these extensions always have an effective encoding [24]. Given the fact that R has an effective encoding if and only if there is a universal R-machine, we conjecture that SAT(R) is in NP(R) if and only if there is a universal R-machine that runs with polynomial-overhead.
context: the proof to obtain Corollary 12 and because we analyze the proof in order to demonstrate that the assumptions of the theorem are probably necessary, or may be weakened only slightly. We conjecture that the assumption that R is of finite type is not strictly necessary because there are structures R of infinite type for which SAT(R) is NP(R) complete, as shown in [34, 24]. However, we have a strong intuition that the existence of an effective encoding for R is a necessary condition for SAT(R) to be in NP(R) because if there is an operation of R that R-machines cannot decode, then R-machines should not be able to test the truth of formulas with this operation. Indeed, the known infinite-type structures for which SAT(R) is NP(R)-complete are Megiddo extensions of finite-type structures, and these extensions always have an effective encoding [24]. Given the fact that R has an effective encoding if and only if there is a universal R-machine, we conjecture that SAT(R) is in NP(R) if and only if there is a universal R-machine that runs with polynomial-overhead. Previously, most research into the polynomial hierarchy over R focused on the cases when R is either Radd = (R, 0, 1, −, +) or Rlin or a number of related structures [9]. Many of the results for the additive reals remain true when R is a ring, and in this case we already knew already that a k-fold quantified version of polynomial feasibility is complete for each level of the polynomial hierarchy over R [3, 6]. Exotic quantifiers are used in [6] to extend the polynomial hierarchy over R in order to achieve completeness results for problems from semialgebraic geometry within these newly defined classes. When restricting to the constant-free Boolean part of these newly defined classes, the exotic quantifiers can be eliminated, thereby yielding completeness results in the Boolean hierarchy over R, which is treated in our next corollary.
